blocks.value: There are two ways to work through part of a 2D array: row processing (loop across one row's columns) and column processing (loop down one column's rows). To touch every element, nest one loop inside the other.
A multidimensional array takes this further: its elements are themselves arrays. A 3D array is essentially groups of 2D arrays:

int[][][] numbers = new int[2][3][5]; // 2 groups, each with 3 rows of 5 elements = 30 elements total
System.out.println(numbers[1][2][3]); // element at group 1, row 2, position 3
